native_result.query: How does the median wealth of white individuals compare to that of black and Hispanic individuals from 1985 onwards?
native_result.HypoA: 1985 onwards, white individuals have a significantly higher median wealth compared to black and Hispanic individuals.
native_result.HypoB:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, natural language):

"From 1985 onwards, the median family net wealth of White individuals in the NLSY79 cohort (operationalized as the non-Black non-Hispanic cohort, since the data file contains no finer race variable) is far higher than that of both Black and Hispanic individuals, and this racial wealth gap widens steadily over time rather than closing. Measured in constant 1996 dollars and including zero and negative net-wealth observations, the White median family net wealth rose from $5,104 (1985) to $15,572 (1990) to $42,600 (1996), while the Black median rose only from $2,333 to $5,762 to $9,800, and the Hispanic median from $729 to $1,921 to $2,562 over the same years. Consequently, the White-to-Black median-wealth ratio widened from about 2.2x (1985) to 2.7x (1990) to 4.3x (1996), and the White-to-Hispanic ratio widened from about 7.0x to 8.1x to 16.6x; the absolute White-Black median gap grew about 12-fold (from roughly $2,800 to $32,800) and the White-Hispanic gap about 9-fold (from roughly $4,400 to $40,000) between 1985 and 1996. All group differences are statistically significant in every year (Mann-Whitney U, all p < 1e-20). A robustness check using a balanced panel of respondents with non-missing wealth in all three years (n=5,739; 1,084 Black, 1,723 Hispanic, 2,932 white proxy) reproduces the same pattern (White-to-Black ratio 2.4x in 1985 to 4.7x in 1996; White-to-Hispanic ~12x to ~18x), confirming the result is not an artifact of differential attrition. Notably, Hispanic median wealth is the lowest of the three groups in every survey year, and Black median wealth exceeds the Hispanic median by roughly 3-4x throughout, so the ordering White > Black > Hispanic (with Hispanic lowest) holds persistently from 1985 onwards."

Key supporting table (headline, year-wise complete cases, constant 1996 USD):
- 1985: White $5,104 (95%CI 4,666-5,395) | Black $2,333 (2,187-2,625) | Hispanic $729 (583-875); W/B ratio 2.19x; W/H 7.00x
- 1990: White $15,572 | Black $5,762 | Hispanic $1,921; W/B 2.70x; W/H 8.11x
- 1996: White $42,600 (40,750-46,000) | Black $9,800 (8,200-11,600) | Hispanic $2,562 (2,000-3,000); W/B 4.35x; W/H 16.62x

Gap trend (constant 1996 USD): White-Black $2,771 (1985) → $9,810 (1990) → $32,800 (1996), ~11.8x growth; White-Hispanic $4,375 → $13,652 → $40,038, ~9.2x growth — absolute gaps widen; relative ratios widen ~2-2.4x.

Caveats stated in the narrative: no finer race variable (white = non-Black non-Hispanic cohort by necessity); unweighted medians because no survey-weight column exists in the file; missing wealth handled via year-wise complete cases plus a balanced-panel robustness check (no imputation); zeros and negative net wealth included; results describe the NLSY79 1957-64 birth cohort, not a full cross-section of the U.S. population.
